title: Article 238 — Application of Part VI to Part B States (Omitted)

content.overview: Article 238 (and the whole of original Part VII) applied Part VI provisions to States in Part B of the First Schedule with modifications. It was omitted by the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956, section 29 and Schedule, with effect from 1 November 1956, when the Part A/B/C/D classification of States was abolished under States reorganisation.
content.glance: Art 238 and Part VII omitted by 7th Amendment 1956 (w.e.f. 1-11-1956). Part B States classification abolished.
content.study:
Before reorganisation, States were classified in Parts A, B, C and D of the First Schedule. Article 238 adapted Part VI (State Government) to Part B States (former princely States under Rajpramukhs).

Omission: Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956, s. 29 and Schedule (w.e.f. 1-11-1956), aligned with the States Reorganisation Act, 1956. The A/B/C/D classification ended; Part B States ceased as a separate constitutional class.

Examination rule: Do not cite Article 238 as living law. Modern State executive and legislature provisions are in Part VI as applicable to all States (subject to special provisions elsewhere).

sections.heading: Constitutional status
sections.body: Omitted by the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956, s. 29 and Schedule (w.e.f. 1-11-1956). Entire original Part VII (‘The States in Part B of the First Schedule’) was removed when linguistic/state reorganisation abolished the Part B category.

sections.heading: Exam checkpoints
sections.body:
1. Link omission to States reorganisation and the end of Part A/B/C/D classification.
2. Do not apply Article 238 to any current State.
3. For current State structure, use Part VI and any special articles (e.g. 371 series) that still apply.

examples.title: Illustration — Post-1956 State structure
examples.body: A question that asks whether Article 238 still modifies Part VI for a former Part B State must be answered in the negative: Article 238 and Part VII were omitted from 1 November 1956.

misconceptions.trap: Article 238 still governs former princely States.
misconceptions.correction: Article 238 was omitted by the 7th Amendment, 1956. The Part B classification no longer exists.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What is the status of Article 238?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Article 238 was omitted by the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956 (w.e.f. 1-11-1956) when Part B States were abolished as a constitutional class. It is not living law.

examTips: Connect 7th Amendment + States Reorganisation Act 1956 + end of Part B States.
